claims.statement: SSHConnectionWorker serializes libssh2 calls on one queue while independent exec state machines and multiplexed SFTP operations share its authenticated session; the PTY worker instantiates the same SFTP owner on its own queue.

The client-side SSH session ceiling defaults to ten and normalizes to 1–100; each physical connection has independent FIFO admission, live decreases do not revoke active channels, and cancellation/close release queued waiters.
Exec acquires and revalidates its connection budget before creating command state; each command has isolated cwd/stdin/output state and a 1–900 second deadline created after channel admission.

Exec serializes pending channel opens and advances opening, startup, running, close and free phases in bounded ready-queue turns; socket events and a 100 ms timer wake work, and output limits count remote bytes independently per stream.

Multiplexed SFTP serializes initialization, retains a session-channel lease per subsystem, performs bounded operations on the enclosing SSH queue, and asynchronously sleeps two milliseconds on EAGAIN rather than using the exec ready dictionary.
SFTPClient owns its primary channel and connection with a generation check, while SFTPChannel siblings reuse the same driver and channel disconnect does not itself close the underlying connection.

Current I/O tuning uses a 256 KiB quantum/read allowance, two-millisecond slice and 2 MiB/1 MiB flow watermarks; immutable chunk storage preserves libssh2 retry pointers and vectored flush avoids coalescing.

SSHConnectionBuffer accepts full encrypted writes and queues unsent remainders to avoid the documented pinned-library forwarding confirmation retry problem, applies receive/pass backpressure, and makes disposal independent of peer I/O.

Socket event cancellation waits for both source cancel handlers before descriptor closure, and exec cleanup changes its generation, fails outstanding commands, closes SFTP and budget, and prevents stale scheduled work from reviving the transport.

AgentConnectionPool reuses Host/route-fingerprint keyed primary SSH and SFTP across tool calls and runs, joins concurrent opens, protects active exec/SFTP operation leases from default 180-second whole-host idle retirement, and retries exec once only for connectionUnavailable before channel start.
SSHExclusiveConnectionAdapter serializes complete operations on one owned connection and has no topology or fallback selection policy.

AgentSSHAuthenticationRegistry shares a per-host temporary authentication context among overlapping operations but releases it with the final caller; authentication configuration attempts join by generation and cancelling the last waiter cancels the shared attempt, while successful authentication consumes staged one-shot secrets.

Agent connection acquisition retries rejected authentication by evicting a pooled connection for normal opens and advancing only the failed authentication generation; SFTP lease acquisition does not evict on this path, while local credential requirements re-resolve configuration without a rejected-auth reset and cancellation or unrelated errors do not enter this retry loop.

Agent route resolution prompts for local proxy/identity/passphrase requirements before network opening; attempts carry host-key and keyboard-interactive callbacks, with failing route-node authentication re-prompted without allowing old-generation failures to erase new credentials.

Agent pool connection-opening waiters cancel independently: the last waiter cancels the shared open, late successful opens are disconnected, and disconnect cancels pending opens; a committed connection uses the post-authentication route fingerprint so identity saves during prompting remain reusable.

Agent pool route changes or missing targets invalidate primary SSH and SFTP reuse; idle sweeping separately retires unused auxiliary SFTP connections and only closes the primary when no active exec or SFTP lease remains, while its connection count includes auxiliary sockets but not sibling subsystem channels.

Agent SFTP operations take exclusive channel leases, use optional file scheduler permits and may acquire auxiliary connections or sibling channels for overlap; acquisition can retry authentication but an already-started operation is not replayed and connection-loss SFTP errors evict the host.

SSHConnectionWorker teardown remains queue-confined even when its last reference is released by an owning-queue callback: deinit cleans up directly on that queue and synchronously dispatches cleanup to it only when released elsewhere, avoiding synchronous self-reentry.

SFTPConcurrencyScheduler accounts one global logical-file permit and one per-host slot for each distinct endpoint, and grants eligible queued work by rotating hosts then sources within a host rather than scheduling libssh2 bytes.

With smart SFTP scheduling, unknown size and files of at most 64,000,000 bytes select channelsOnly while larger files select connectionsPreferred; the permit's scheduling mode is distinct from session-channel admission.
